title: Three-day date delays permitted both warmth slope signs for birch and beech leaf order in four Swiss samples in 1996-2025
abstract: We tested whether April warmth relative to March was linked to beech leaf unfolding before birch. We used 2,615 matched station-years at 104 Swiss stations in two regions and two periods. Recorded-order slopes were positive, from 1.03 to 2.96 percentage points per C. All four family intervals from station and three-year block resampling included zero. Under separate species reporting delays of up to three days, sharp fixed-record slope bounds permitted both signs in every sample. Only 17-34 percent of weighted records had an uncertain order at this delay cap. Small delays on tied dates alone permitted both signs in the early samples under a continuous date model. These bounds require correct phase reports and errors within the assumed delay range. They are not confidence intervals. The study does not establish a common change in true leaf order. The regions share weather and one reporting network. Monthly weather can follow the leaf event. Pollution, daily extremes, competition and ecological harm were not measured. Code, source hashes, aggregate evidence and independent numerical checks are included.

display.caption: Recorded-order slopes and four-test family intervals at left. Sharp fixed-record slope bounds under separate species date delays at right. Three-day bounds permit both signs in all four samples.
